sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Every Brucebase preview window on brucebase.wikidot.com ends with a folded "History" section: the page's revisions, newest first (number, date, who, the kind of change, the comment), and what the revision you click changed — the old lines and the new ones side by side, the changed words marked, the unchanged lines folded ("Everything" shows them), a revision that changed only tags or the title saying so. You need not be signed in: the wiki answers its history to everyone (probed signed in and signed out). Nothing is read until the section opens; then 20 revisions ("Load 20 more" for older ones) and the two texts the change needs, one request a second, kept until you leave the page. ✎ in the window's title bar and H open it; on a page that has a window, the ☰ menu's "✎ Page history" opens it for the page itself. Setting: Page history in the Brucebase window (on).

sections.label: 📝 Docs
items: Help: the window's History section; two places still named the event preview setting by its old label.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase release and playlist pages get a button, "Release": a table per edition and disc (song, running time, where the track comes from, the page's footnote on it; a box set's films each a table of their own), the personnel, the related releases, a live release's recording dates (the show's date and place, linked), the takes On The Tracks and how often each song was played live. Above them the facts the page states (released, label, produced, recorded, mixed, mastered, design, photography), each edition's running time, the overview, footnotes and history, tags, media, the lyrics' pages and the artwork typed by its file names; the wiki's page folded below. Nothing is fetched.

Brucebase bootleg pages get "Bootleg": the tracklist, a table per disc with each song's time and, where the page marks them, the sides; the label, catalog number, time, format, source and sound in a Bootleg card, the notes and the Front, Back and Disc artwork. The wiki writes bootlegs as free text — lists, numbered lines, "Disc 1: (43:31)", "//" after a side's last song — and all of it is read.

Links to Brucebase release, playlist and bootleg pages preview them (Ctrl+hover): their facts and tracks; Space opens the window with the overview, personnel and related releases. The settings are now called "Detail pages: events, songs, venues, people, releases and bootlegs as tables" and "Preview event, venue, people, release and bootleg pages on hover".

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: A YouTube player embedded as "youtube.com/embed/playlist?list=…" (Brucebase's release pages) was taken for a video named "playlist"; it is the playlist.
Brucebase On The Tracks: a take written "THE HEIST - V2 - take 14" or "JUNGLELAND - V1 (August 1, 1974)" is now split into title and version too (song pages and the new release pages).

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: the shows in a person's lists link the wiki's "on stage" pages, which the wiki forwards to the show; these links now preview the show itself, card and window.

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: A new WARNING on the Brucebase detail pages, "Brucebase entry with a comma after its date": an entry the wiki lists as "2015-04-30, Story Chapel, …" instead of "2015-04-30 Story Chapel, …". It is still read; the Date cell is tinted, its tooltip quotes the entry, and the lists being the linked pages' titles, that page's title is the one to fix. Settings "Find Brucebase entries with a comma after their date" and its highlight (both on).

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase venue pages get a button, "Venue": the performances, cancelled shows and appearances at the venue as tables, its description, region, count, map link and pictures above, the wiki's page folded below.

Brucebase pages of people and bands get "Person": every performance with Bruce Springsteen as one table — the wiki splits long lists into pages (Steven Van Zandt's 1,517 shows over six), and every page is read, one request each — with an As column saying in which band; the count per band; appearances; the recordings by song and role; their bands or members (in reading order: "The E Street Band"); songs co-written with Bruce. The biography, tags and pictures are above. The setting is now called "Detail pages: events, songs, venues and people as tables".

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase song pages get a button, "Song": the credits (each release, who played what), the performances counted by tour (only the tours it was played on, with its share of the shows), every performance, multiple performances on one date, snippets, the official live downloads and its takes On The Tracks (title, take, running time, the bootlegs and releases it is on), as tables you can filter and sort. Above them: where the song comes from, Released on Album, the lyrics and notes (folded), a Song card (how often and when last played live, released on, live downloads, takes), its tags, media and links; the wiki's page folded below. An On The Tracks page gets "Versions": its takes as one table. Nothing is fetched. The setting is now called "Detail pages: events and songs as tables".

sections.label: 🚀 Feature
items: Brucebase event pages (a gig, a show that did not happen, a recording session, a rehearsal, an interview) get a button, "Event", that lays the page out like a MusicBrainz release, from the page itself with nothing fetched. Above the tables: what it was, where and when; About this show; an Event card (type, date and weekday, scheduled time, venue, tour, the year page, running time), the page's tags by family and its YouTube links; the pictures with a chip per kind and per photographer. The tables: the Setlist as one table (Set, #, Song in MusicBrainz style, Segue, Premiere ★ for a song in bold on the wiki, Note), who was on stage with their band and role, the other shows at the venue (this one in bold), the recordings (official releases, bootlegs with their labels, the live download) and the Storyteller's words by song. The wiki's own page stays below, folded, its headings folding too. Setting "Event pages: a detail view of the gig" (on). Mockup: https://claude.ai/artifact/3rAGVKsBHEv9jGspkJ5X7Z

sections.label: 🐛 Fix
items: Brucebase previews: the scheduled time is read on pages that write it "Scheduled: 21:00 | Local Start Time …" too; the card left it out.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase previews: a picture now says what its file name tells, the photographer included ("Photo · Cliff Breining · #01", "Setlist · #01a · Handwritten", "Pass · #01 · Backstage"), in the window and in the full-size viewer. The window shows the photos once per photographer, those without a known photographer last. Each group folds on a click on its heading, and a Ctrl+click folds or opens every group at once, so a gig with hundreds of photos can be folded away; the text sections stay as they are.

Brucebase previews: the window ends with the page's tags, folded at first, sorted into Date, Place, Tour, On the page, Songs, People, Releases and more; each tag links to the wiki's list of pages with it. Previews already cached are read once more.

sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Brucebase: the side bar's show/hide handle now sits at the top of the side bar, as the MusicBrainz sidebar's does, instead of halfway down the window. Scrolled down, it stays near the top of the window; with the side bar hidden, it sits at the top of the page content.
